items.title: Demand Rising in the Ship Recycling Markets
points: Best Oasis added that “the Pakistani ship recycling market remained largely unchanged this week, with subdued buying interest amid sluggish domestic market conditions.
Continued pressure from Iranian imports, including unofficial cross-border trade, has further dampened breakers’ appetite for acquiring vessels.
Finally, the Turkish ship recycling market remains cautious, with limited vessel availability and weak purchasing activity.
No new recycling sales were reported during the week, as yards continued to face pressure from weak domestic steel demand, high financing costs and currency depreciation.
Buying prices remain relatively uncompetitive compared with India, Bangladesh and Pakistan, limiting Türkiye’s ability to attract conventional recycling tonnage.

On the policy front, the European Parliament’s Environmental Committee voted against the proposal to include the 2 Indian yards on the EU approval list, citing concerns over beaching methods, although a final decision is still pending.
In policy, Pakistan reached to 6 authorized ship recycling facilities by HKC and DASR requirements.
Nikos Roussanoglou, Hellenic Shipping News Worldwide

items.title: Tankers In High Demand During October
points: Disclosed investment across all sectors reached approximately US$4.7bn, below September’s US$6.6bn.
Tankers attracted US$2.9bn, compared with US$1.1bn for dry bulk and US$0.7bn for other vessels.
Their share was approximately 62% of total capital, rising to 73% within dry bulk and tankers alone.
Through October, total sales reached 1,481 vessels, up 17% year on year.
Dry bulk retained the larger count, with 644 sales against 572 tankers, but tanker purchases grew 68%, compared with 7% for dry bulk.
Tankers also attracted US$20.8bn of the US$32.1bn disclosed across these two sectors, versus US$11.3bn for dry bulk.
Within dry bulk and tankers, Greek buyers purchased 16 ships in October, evenly split between the sectors; Chinese buyers purchased 12, comprising nine bulkers and three tankers.
Over January–October, Greek capital favoured tankers, at US$4.5bn against US$2.1bn in dry bulk.

items.title: Shipping puts AI readiness to the test with new maturity benchmark
points: Unveiled at Smart Maritime Network Singapore 2026, the enhanced DMI process introduces AI readiness benchmarking and sector-specific digital use cases while marking a milestone of more than 100 participating organisations.

Developed to help maritime organisations benchmark their digital capabilities against industry peers, the DMI enables organisations to assess current capabilities, prioritise investment and accelerate progress towards their digital ambitions.

The new AI maturity assessment examines the foundations required for successful AI adoption, including governance, workforce training, organisational culture, data readiness and performance measurement.

By looking beyond technology adoption alone, the assessment helps organisations identify whether they have the people, processes and data infrastructure needed to support AI-driven decision making and operational improvement.
“The DMI helps organisations establish that baseline.
Constantinos Chaelis, Gas Segment Director, LR, said: “For LNG operators, digital transformation needs to be grounded in the operational realities of gas shipping.

items.title: Global Shipping Report: October U.S. Container Imports Hit Record Volume
points: U.S. containerized imports totaled 2,674,808 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in October 2026, up 5.0% from September and 16.0% from October 2025.
October marked the highest monthly volume on record, exceeding the previous high set in May 2022 by 2.0%.
U.S. containerized imports increased by 128,547 TEUs (5.0%) from September to 2,674,808 TEUs in October 2026 (see Figure 1).
Figure 1: U.S. Container Import Volume Year-over-Year Comparison September-to-October volumes increased in nine of the 11 years since 2016 (see Figure 2).
Figure 2: September to October U.S. Container Import Volume Comparison Top 10 U.S. port volumes rise as East and Gulf Coast entries gain.
Combined imports across the top 10 U.S. ports increased 4.5% (98,272 TEUs) from September to October 2026 (see Figure 3).
New York, NY, increased 16.6% (9,081 TEUs), Tacoma 4.8% (3,292 TEUs), and New York/Newark (Newark, NJ) 0.3% (863 TEUs).
Three West Coast ports declined: Los Angeles fell 1.4% (7,310 TEUs), Long Beach 2.0% (10,156 TEUs), and Oakland 10.9% (8,714 TEUs).

items.title: Midterms strip out the war premium, but the next two months make shorts a risky bet
points: Brent fell 16.6% between the 30 October peak and 4 November.
On that day the January contract settled at $94.62/bbl after an $8.98/bbl drop.
Brent has since rebounded to around $97/bbl amid fresh tanker incidents in the Hormuz Strait, and prompt spreads have firmed, but it remains on course for a weekly loss of roughly 12%.
The DFL spread collapsed from as much as +$18/bbl to +$1.70/bbl over the month (Argus) and the North Sea Dated M1-M2 spread fell to -$3.20/bbl on 4 November, its weakest since May 2020.
Dubai M1-M2 flipped into contango for the first time since mid-July, and Murban’s premium to Dubai swaps shrank to $4.50/bbl from more than $30/bbl in mid-September (Argus).
Aramco cut its December Arab Light OSP to Asia by $2/bbl to a six-year low, below the market at roughly Oman/Dubai -$7/bbl.

items.title: Eni, Fincantieri and RINA present the second edition of the Sustainable Maritime Transport Outlook
points: The Outlook provides a global overview of solutions for decarbonising maritime transport, comparing different technology and fuel options in terms of their emissions reduction potential, maturity, infrastructure availability and the evolution of their…
The key message emerging from this second edition is that the landscape is more uncertain than it was a year ago.

Under the Outlook’s reference scenario, “Today as Future”, Europe is expected to achieve an 80% reduction in emissions intensity by 2050 compared with 2020 levels, while the reduction globally is projected at around 40%.

The Outlook also considers a slower scenario, “Decarbonization by 2070”, under which the achievement of Europe’s decarbonisation targets is postponed until 2070, with countries in the rest of the world following several years later.

The global IMO agreement has been postponed and, when countries are weighted by tonnage, almost 90% support a more gradual pathway, while the United States has taken a position against maritime decarbonisation.

items.title: Europe’s Pitch Book: Italy – the resilient Nonna
points: Why would we include this country in Europe’s Pitchbook – a series intended to make you see Europe’s strengths and opportunities, rather than only the weaknesses and risks?
At some 1,700 hours per worker per year, the country ranks 12th among OECD countries, well above Germany, Switzerland, the Netherlands and the Nordics.
Among 55- to 64-year-olds, labour participation increased by 30 percentage points between 2004 and 2024.
Among women, the country saw a 14 percentage point increase in participation.
In 2024, 65% of women between 25 and 54 were working, implying Italy was much closer to the European average.
In December 2014, Italian banks had a non-performing loan ratio of 17%.
Today, that ratio stands at 1.9%, exactly in line with the European average.
Since 2012, the country has been on a long deleveraging trajectory, with credit to the corporate sector declining rapidly relative to GDP.

items.title: FUJAIRAH DATA: Oil product stockpiles drop for first time in four weeks
points: Oil product stockpiles at Fujairah in the UAE dropped 10% in the week ended Nov.
9, led by a 25% decline in heavy distillates used as ship fuel and for power generation, according to Fujairah Oil Industry Zone data published Nov.
Total inventory fell to 10.222 million barrels, marking the first decline in four weeks after reaching its highest level since April 6 a week earlier, FOIZ data showed.
Heavy distillate stocks declined to 4.429 million barrels, the first drop in four weeks.

Inventories of light distillates, such as gasoline and naphtha, fell 17% to 2.756 million barrels, the first drop in five weeks, while stocks of middle distillates, including jet fuel and diesel, rose 35% to 3.037 million barrels, the highest since Feb.

items.title: UAC reaches global growth milestone with first international MEGC shipment from China
points: UMOE Advanced Composites (UAC) has completed manufacture of five Multi Element Gas Containers (MEGCs) at its Jiaxing facility in China and is shipping the MEGCs to the Hiringa Sundown Joint Venture in Australia.
The shipment marks UAC’s first international commercial delivery of MEGCs from its China manufacturing facility.
It is also a technology milestone, with the MEGCs incorporating the first Type IV glass-fibre pressure cylinders manufactured in China.
The two 20-foot and three 40-foot MEGCs will support the Good Earth Green Hydrogen and Ammonia (GEGHA) Project in New South Wales.

The project is being developed by Hiringa Sundown, a joint venture between Hiringa Energy and Sundown Pastoral Company, and will use green hydrogen and low-carbon ammonia to help decarbonize agriculture and transport.
The shipment is an important step in UAC’s global growth strategy, moving its Jiaxing facility from production ramp-up into commercial delivery for international customers.

items.title: New Gard tool provides fleet insights into sensitive marine areas
points: Whales and other marine mammals follow ancient migration routes across the world’s oceans.

Gard’s new portal feature enables Members and clients to visualise how their trading routes interact with Important Marine Mammal Areas (IMMAs) and generate metrics to support decision-making and sustainability reporting.
From general guidance to fleet-specific insights For many years, Gard has shared best practice and operational guidance on whales and other marine mammals through its series of insight articles.
This new feature builds on that work by analysing fleet trading patterns in relation to Important Marine Mammal Areas.
These areas are identified through a rigorous, expert driven process led by the International Union for the Conservation of Nature (IUCN).

These include the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS), the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB), and the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD).

He subsequently held senior executive positions, including Chief Operating Officer and Chief Executive Officer, respectively with established Greek shipping companies Eletson Corporation and Aegean Shipping Management, gaining extensive experience in ship…

items.title: Fund for Energy Efficiency Technologies (FEET) is the first fund to adopt the Singapore-Asia Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance
points: The Fund for Energy Efficiency Technologies (FEET) has adopted the second edition of the Singapore-Asia Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (SAT) to guide investment decisions, making FEET the first fund to adopt the SAT.
The Singapore Sustainable Finance Association (SSFA), supported by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), announced the second edition of the SAT at COP31 in Türkiye.

The Global Centre for Maritime Decarbonisation (GCMD) also announced that Lloyd’s Register (LR) has completed its independent review of the Centre’s methodology for quantifying fuel savings from WAPS, which underpins FEET’s financing of these projects.
It offers up to 100% upfront financing through a blended finance structure.
FEET is managed by AIM Horizon Investments, with GCMD as the fund’s decarbonisation advisor, and is supported by the Development Bank of Japan, DBS Bank and ING.
Professor Lynn Loo, CEO of GCMD, joined the COP31 panel “Stocktake and the Path Ahead: Facilitating Transition Finance in Asia Pacific” at the Singapore Pavilion.

items.title: Everllence Two-Stroke Dual-Fuel Technology Selected for Landmark Indian Chemical-Tanker Project
points: Everllence has received an order from Swan Defence and Heavy Industries Limited (SDHI), India’s largest shipbuilding and heavy engineering company, for two-stroke, dual-fuel engine technology.
The engines will power a series of six 18,000-dwt IMO Type II chemical tankers.
The project represents SDHI’s first two-stroke newbuild contract following the revitalisation of India’s largest shipyard by capacity at Pipavav, Gujarat.
The project, which is also India’s first order for chemical tankers, reflects India’s growing ambition in commercial shipbuilding.

The first vessel in the tanker series will be powered by an Everllence B&W 6S50ME-C9.7-GI-EGRBP two-stroke engine, manufactured by longstanding Everllence licensee, MITSUI E&S Co. , Ltd. The engine will furthermore be equipped with exhaust-gas…
The 18,000-dwt vessels are intended for demanding North European operations and will be built to Ice Class 1A requirements.

Having recently celebrated 100 years of continuous two-stroke licensing cooperation with Everllence, we will draw on our extensive experience and expertise in manufacturing large marine engines to work closely with Everllence and SDHI on this project.

items.title: Dollar climbs as traders raise December Fed hike bets
points: NEW YORK, Nov 11 (Reuters) - The dollar strengthened against major currencies on Wednesday, buoyed by growing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates after hot US inflation data and hawkish remarks from policymakers.

Traders have boosted bets on a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December to 87% from about 70% a month ago, according to CME's FedWatch Tool, after US consumer prices rose more than expected in October for a third consecutive month.

The rise in rate expectations is helping support the dollar, said Elias Haddad, global head of markets strategy at Brown Brothers Harriman & Co. The dollar rose 0.69% to 159.84 against the Japanese yen , hitting its strongest in over two months and nearing…
The euro dropped 0.65% to $1.11, extending losses from the prior session and hitting its lowest since May 2025.

items.title: CME cattle futures end mixed after two-day rebound from multi-month lows
points: CHICAGO, Nov 11 (Reuters) - Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures ended mixed on Wednesday, with actively traded nearby contracts pressured by profit taking and technical selling following two sessions of strong gains.
Tight cattle supplies and improving packer margins underpinned the market, while feeder cattle futures posted modest gains as feed corn prices eased.
Before rebounding this week, both markets had been on a two-week slide that dragged prices to multi-month lows, leaving them poised for a technical rebound.
"It feels more like a technical correction of an oversold market than an absolute turn in the market," said Jim McCormick, chief operating officer at AgMarket.
CME December live cattle settled 0.225 cent higher at 218.975 cents per pound.
The benchmark contract touched its lowest level since December 2 on Friday.
January feeder cattle held technical support at its 100-day moving average but failed to break through chart resistance at its 50-day average.

items.title: Canada Pension Aims to Double Hedge Fund Bets to $160 Billion
points: (Bloomberg) -- Canada’s largest pension is planning to roughly double the money it invests in hedge funds over the next five to seven years, a bullish signal from one of the industry’s most important backers.
The Canada Pension Plan Investment Board plans to boost its total hedge fund allocation to about $160 billion in the coming years, according to people familiar with the matter.

It is particularly interested in gaining exposure to hedge fund giants it doesn’t currently invest with, including Izzy Englander’s Millennium Management, said the people, asking not to be named discussing internal deliberations.
The C$866 billion ($608 billion) pension currently has about $80 billion invested in hedge funds, according to the people.

External hedge fund investments were largely responsible for the $3.4 billion of net income generated by its Capital Markets and Factor Investing segment in the 12 months ended March, according to CPPIB’s annual report.

items.title: Keralam government centralising power in Chief Minister’s office: Pinarayi Vijayan
points: Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan has accused the Keralam government of concentrating decision-making powers in the hands of the Chief Minister, alleging that even ministers are being kept in the dark about important decisions.
He said the situation was unprecedented in the State and called for a judicial investigation into what he described as suspicious administrative actions.

Speaking at the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] political explanation meeting at Chathurakkinar in Madikkai, Mr. Vijayan questioned how a Minister, who is also the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee president, could remain unaware of major…
He said governance was being conducted without proper coordination between departments, with the Chief Minister taking decisions independently.
Referring to the electricity purchase agreement with GNA, Mr. Vijayan said the Minister concerned had earlier said that he was unaware of the decision to enter into the agreement.
The Minister was reportedly unaware even when the decision to abandon the agreement was taken, he said.

items.title: Great Trigonometrical Survey stations in Tamil Nadu documented, published in five volumes
points: The Department of Survey and Settlement and the Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology have documented the Great Trigonometrical Survey (GTS) stations in the State and published the documentation in five volumes.
According to an official release, during British rule, the Great Trigonometrical Survey was launched by Colonel William Lambton at St. Thomas Mount in Chennai on April 10, 1802.
The survey continued for 70 years until 1871 using theodolite instruments.
As part of the exercise, Great Trigonometrical Survey stations were established across India, including at several locations in Tamil Nadu.
The Tamil Nadu government granted permission for a comprehensive exercise to identify all the GTS stations in the State, conduct surveys, map and document them, and take steps to preserve them.
Accordingly, officials from the Department of Survey and Settlement and TNSDA jointly conducted an extensive field survey, identified all the GTS stations in Tamil Nadu and documented their details.

items.title: Geneva Dry: Belships’ Ivar Hansson Myklebust on China’s changing commodities role
points: Ivar Hansson Myklebust, chair and CEO of Norway’s Belships, believes the shipping industry continues to underestimate the growth potential of developing economies.
Ahead of his appearance at Geneva Dry 2027, he discusses China’s changing trading patterns, fleet supply and the opportunities emerging across minor bulks.

A changing China, resilient emerging economies and a relatively predictable fleet supply picture will be among the biggest themes shaping dry bulk shipping when the industry gathers in Geneva next April, according to Ivar Hansson Myklebust.
The Belships chief is cautiously optimistic about the outlook for minor bulks, arguing that developing economies continue to generate more trade than many shipping forecasts anticipate.
Before joining Belships, he headed OMP Management and held senior leadership positions at Höegh Autoliners and Norden.
Myklebust will join the Minor Bulks panel at Geneva Dry on Wednesday, April 28, alongside Emilie Nourry of Eramet, Malgorzata Gill of Holcim Trading, S.K.
Lim of G2 Ocean and Vincenzo Romeo of Nova Marine Carriers.

"More importantly, even if a political agreement is reached, shipping activity is unlikely to return to normal immediately." Brent and WTI prices have fallen about 21% and 17%, respectively, since the start of the month on hopes of an end to the war.

items.title: Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng says she has been stopped from coming to Hyderabad for Bharat Summit
points: Screenshot from video posted by Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng (X/@HelleLyngSvends) on November 11, 2026, in which she says that her visa to visit India was “cancelled”.
Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng, who works for the Oslo-based daily newspaper Dagsavisen, has said that she has been stopped from coming to India despite having a valid visa.
“I got a visa to India and was supposed to leave this morning to attend the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad.
But «orders from above» in the Ministry of Home Affairs have cancelled my visa,” she said in a post on X, on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

“I was supposed to speak on media, press freedom and democracy and how they are intertwined,” she spoke in the video message where she puts the onus on India’s Home Minister Amit Shah to let her come as 48 hours are still there for her session.
I got a visa to India and was supposed to leave this morning to attend the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad.

items.title: Russian Diesel Tanker Makes U-Turn After Heading to U.S.
points: (Bloomberg) — A tanker carrying Russian diesel that had briefly signaled the US made a U-turn about 400 nautical miles off New York, compounding uncertainty over deliveries to the North American market.

The Agioi Fanendes, hauling about 40,000 metric tons of ultralow-sulfur diesel, or almost 300,000 barrels, started to move away from the US East Coast and has been dawdling in a zigzag pattern since Monday, according to a port report and ship-tracking data…
Traders are closely watching movements of Russian diesel after President Vladimir Putin agreed to supply fuel to the US and global markets in a deal with President Donald Trump last month.
The arrangement sparked criticism from US Democrats, who argued it would help the Kremlin finance its war in Ukraine, and so far no Russian diesel cargo has reached America, tracking data show.
Russia said last month it had loaded four tankers with diesel destined for the US, in line with the Putin-Trump agreement, according to Interfax.

items.title: Karnataka Minister Eshwar Khandre asks officials to blacklist Larsen & Toubro for ‘delaying’ works
points: Minister for Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Eshwar Khandre Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar Khandre has directed that Larsen & Toubro Limited (L&T) be blacklisted for alleged slow progress of work in drinking water projects.

The direction came after the final notice issued to the company that is executing drinking water facilities to 388 rural habitations in Dharwad district, Kalghatgi town, and eight en route rural habitations of Saundatti taluk, Belagavi district from the…
Sources said that though the work was awarded on April 20, 2022, to be completed by October 19, 2024, the progress on site was very slow.
The daily pipeline progress is also less than 500 m per day, sources said.

Sources said that the officials informed the Minister during a meeting that despite the instructions, pipes allegedly had not been purchased, adequate number of workers had not been deployed and work was progressing slow, and that progress report was not…

items.title: Crushing begins at Tiruttani Cooperative Sugarmills
points: The Tiruttani Cooperative Sugarmills will crush over two lakh tonnes of sugarcane grown by 1,767 farmers on 7,601 acres of land in 2025-27.
Gandhiraj flagged off the crushing on Wednesday at a function in Tiruttani, with Minister for AI and IT R.
Kumar, Tiruttani MLA Arunkumar, and Tiruvallur District Collector S.
Joseph Vijay had announced a special incentive of ₹709.50 per tonne.
Last year, 1,647 farmers had brought in 2.03 tonnes of sugarcane to be crushed, said a press release.

items.title: MP alleges intelligence failure over Nanjangud drug racket
points: Mysuru-Kodagu MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar has accused the Congress government of a serious intelligence failure following the alleged busting of an inter-State drug racket operating under the guise of a banana plantation in Nanjangud by the…

In a statement here, Mr. Yaduveer said it was shocking that the racket operating on Karnataka soil was detected by the police of a neighbouring State rather than the Karnataka Police or the State intelligence wing.

He said this was not an isolated incident, pointing out that Maharashtra Police and central investigating agencies had intervened in recent years to expose organised drug networks operating in Mysuru.
“Such incidents raised serious questions about the effectiveness of the State’s intelligence machinery,” he added.

He alleged that the repeated involvement of police forces from other States and central agencies in detecting alleged criminal networks operating in Karnataka reflected serious lapses in law enforcement and intelligence gathering.
The Congress government should take moral responsibility for the failure, he demanded.

items.title: No Rain, No Relief: Weather Chief Dashes Pollution-Hit Delhi's Hopes
points: The northern plains are choking from pollution and a billion Indians living there are looking at the skies.
There might be some over the Himalayan region, but none is expected in Delhi, where the pollution has reached severe levels.
This also ruins the IIT Kanpur's cloud seeding plan, India Meteorological Department chief Dr Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, told NDTV.
What is expected to bring rains over Himalayas is a Western disturbance -- a moisture-laden weather pattern that emerges from the Mediterranean Sea and comes from the west.
The Western Disturbance will bring rain and snowfall in Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
Delhi could be overcast on November 12 and 13, but there will not be enough precipitation.
The possibility of a cloud seeding operation is being considered by researchers from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Kanpur and the Delhi Government.
According to the IMD, a deep depression is expected to form around November 15 or 16, which could intensify into a cyclonic storm.

items.title: Swachh Survekshan: Guntur wins ‘Super Swachh League’ award
points: Guntur Municipal Corporation Commissioner K.
Mayur Ashok received the award from President Droupadi Murmu at a ceremony held at Vigyan Bhavan in New Delhi on Wednesday, along with Municipal Administration and Urban Development Minister P.
Suresh Kumar and APTIDCO Managing Director B.
Andhra Pradesh has secured six national awards, emerging as the second-best performing State in the country.
Mr. Ashok attributed the achievement to the collective efforts of municipal officials, sanitation workers and public participation.
A waste-to-energy plant is operational, while a Letter of Award has been issued for establishing a new Bio-CBG plant to generate green energy from waste.
Scientific removal of legacy waste, the ‘Swarnandhra-Swachh Andhra’ programme and the 30-day ‘Operation Clean Sweep’ drive contributed to improving urban cleanliness, he said.
The Municipal Commissioner pledged to continue efforts to transform Guntur into a cleaner and better-maintained city.

items.title: U.S. Ethanol Could Fuel Growing Fleet of Methanol-Capable Ships, Study Finds
points: A new study says the United States has enough spare ethanol production capacity to supply a meaningful share of the global marine fuel market, offering shipowners another fuel option as the number of methanol-capable vessels continues to grow.
According to the study, more than 300 methanol-capable vessels are already operating or on order, creating a potential market for ethanol either as a standalone marine fuel or blended with methanol.

The country already accounts for slightly more than half of global fuel ethanol production and exports to approximately 80 countries, supported by an established distribution network that includes Gulf Coast terminals near major bunkering hubs.

The study estimates that supplying just 1% of shipping’s annual fuel consumption by mass would require approximately 1 billion gallons of ethanol, an amount that could be covered by existing U.S. spare capacity.
A 5% market share by the mid-2030s would require around 5 billion gallons annually, necessitating additional production or a shift in existing demand.

items.title: Delhi Boy Falls Into Sewer, Dismembered Body Found In Water Treatment Plant
points: A nearly 24-hour rescue operation to find a four-year-old boy who fell into an open sewer in the Baprola area here ended tragically on Wednesday when the team found the child's dismembered body at a water treatment plant in Nilothi, police said.
Police suspect the body was dismembered by the large rotating machines that filter and treat wastewater at the sewage treatment plant.

The child fell into the manhole near Kheri Baba Pul in Nangli Vihar Extension on Tuesday afternoon, triggering an extensive search operation involving the Delhi Police, fire brigade personnel, local divers and the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF).
The rescue teams followed the sewer and drain route and eventually reached the Water Treatment Plant in Nilothi, Nihal Vihar, where the child's body was found in multiple parts, police said.

items.title: Russian Diesel Faces U.S. Buyer Resistance Despite Trump Sanctions Waiver
points: HOUSTON, Nov 11 (Reuters) – US companies are unlikely to import Russian diesel as a tanker full of the fuel idles off the US Eastern Seaboard, experts said, despite President Donald Trump’s temporary waiver of some sanctions on Moscow’s fuel exports.
Former President Joe Biden imposed the sanctions after the 2022 invasion, and Congress later backed them and codified them as law.

Looking to lower diesel prices that spiked during the US-Israeli war on Iran, Trump’s plan would allow Russia to immediately export 300,000 tons, or 2.25 million barrels, of diesel to US and global markets.

This would be followed by 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons “immediately thereafter.” The price of diesel in the US was $6.13 per gallon on Wednesday, according to the American Automobile Association.
That is down 20 cents a gallon from $6.33 the day that Trump waived the sanctions in October but up 63% from $3.76 before the US-Israeli war on Iran began in late February, according to AAA data.

items.title: Collegium wants transfer of HC judges streamlined, random ways discarded
points: The Supreme Court collegium is working to establish a systematic policy for transferring judges among high courts.
Currently, transfers are largely subject to personal criteria, which the collegium aims to revise.

This new policy emphasizes objective reasoning to streamline the transfer process, reduce personal biases, and enhance accountability regarding judges’ conduct and expertise, marking a pivotal evolution in judicial integrity management.

items.title: SC: Indians married here can't get divorced abroad
points: In a landmark decision, the Supreme Court declared that divorces executed overseas, based on grounds not acknowledged under Indian law, are invalid.
This ruling implies that individuals who remarry after such foreign divorces may risk prosecution for bigamy.
The court also affirmed that marriages conducted according to Indian traditions hold validity, irrespective of any foreign citizenship.

items.title: Complete data could've raised average Diwali pollution level 49%
points: On Diwali night, the absence of PM2.5 data from monitoring stations led to distorted pollution readings in Delhi.
Research by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air indicated that pollution levels might have increased by as much as 49%.
While the Central Pollution Control Board pointed out calibration limitations, readings from the Delhi Pollution Control Committee were inconsistent.

Cooter emphasized that new international student policies focus on eliminating fraudulent schools while still welcoming legitimate Indian student applications.

items.title: Green energy push helped India save $100bn over last 15 yrs: IEA
points: India's remarkable leap in renewable energy capacity has led to over $100 billion in reduced costs for coal and natural gas imports.
With 300GW of renewable power, the nation stands as the second-fastest-growing market worldwide.
The International Energy Agency estimates that by 2030, cumulative savings could soar to $240 billion.
